item.content:encoded:
The UNICEF USA Club Registration for the 2026–2027 school year is now open for students and schools interested in taking action for children in the United States and around the world.

The initiative provides an opportunity for students to establish or continue a UNICEF Club and participate in activities that support child rights, awareness, advocacy, fundraising, and UNICEF’s broader mission for children.

Both new and returning UNICEF Clubs are required to complete the official registration process in order to be recognized as active UNICEF Clubs for the 2026–2027 school year.

What Is the UNICEF USA Club Registration?

The UNICEF USA Club Registration is the official process through which schools and student groups register a UNICEF Club for the upcoming academic year.

UNICEF USA works with communities and young people to build awareness and support for children’s rights. Through UNICEF Clubs, students can organize activities and campaigns that help raise awareness about issues affecting children and encourage their peers and communities to become involved.

For the 2026–2027 school year, UNICEF USA is inviting both newly established and returning clubs to complete the registration form.

Registration is important because a club must be approved by the UNICEF USA team before it can become an active UNICEF Club.

Who Should Consider Registering?

The registration opportunity is particularly relevant to:

  • Students interested in children’s rights and global development.
  • Students who want to organize a UNICEF Club at their school.
  • Existing UNICEF Clubs returning for the 2026–2027 school year.
  • Student leaders interested in advocacy and community engagement.
  • School communities interested in supporting UNICEF’s mission.
  • Individuals who want to raise awareness about challenges facing children around the world.
  • Students who want practical experience in leadership, organization, communication, teamwork, advocacy, and community activities.

Whether you are establishing a UNICEF Club for the first time or continuing an existing club, UNICEF USA states that both new and returning clubs must complete the registration form.

What Can a UNICEF Club Do?

A UNICEF Club can provide students with a structured platform to become involved in issues affecting children.

Depending on the activities organized by a particular club, students may have opportunities to:

  1. Raise awareness about children’s rights.
  2. Educate fellow students about challenges affecting children.
  3. Organize school or community activities.
  4. Support UNICEF-related campaigns.
  5. Encourage advocacy for children.
  6. Participate in fundraising or awareness initiatives.
  7. Develop leadership and organizational skills.
  8. Work collaboratively with other students and an advisor.
  9. Engage their school community around issues affecting children.
  10. Connect local student action with UNICEF’s work for children around the world.

The club structure can therefore be particularly valuable for students who want to combine education, leadership and community involvement.

Requirements Before Starting the Registration

One of the most important things prospective applicants should know is that the registration form requires information about the club’s leadership and advisor.

UNICEF USA requires the contact information of:

  • Four club leaders
  • One club advisor

Applicants should therefore collect all necessary contact information before starting the registration form.

This is especially important because UNICEF USA states that there is no save-and-return option on the registration form.

In other words, applicants should make sure they have the required information available before beginning the application.

Information You Should Prepare

Before accessing the registration form, prospective clubs should have the details of their four club leaders and one advisor ready.

It is advisable to verify the information carefully before submitting the form to avoid unnecessary delays or mistakes.

Applicants should also make sure that everyone involved understands their role within the club and is prepared to provide accurate contact information.

UNICEF Club Registration Process

The UNICEF USA registration page contains a multi-stage webform. The registration process is organized into several sections.

According to the registration page, applicants will move through the following stages:

1. Find Your School or Organization

The first stage involves identifying the school or organization associated with the UNICEF Club.

Applicants should provide the requested information so UNICEF USA can associate the club with the appropriate educational institution or organization.

2. Get Started

After identifying the school or organization, applicants proceed to the next stage of the registration process.

This section begins the formal club registration questionnaire.

3. Questionnaire

Applicants will complete the questionnaire provided as part of the UNICEF Club registration process.

It is important to read each question carefully and provide accurate information.

4. Advisor Information

The registration process requires information about the club’s advisor.

As noted by UNICEF USA, each club must provide information for one advisor.

Prospective clubs should therefore have their advisor’s required information available before starting.

5. Enter Your Leader Information

This section requires information about the club’s student leaders.

UNICEF USA requires contact information for four club leaders.

Clubs should therefore select their leadership team and collect the required information before beginning the registration form.

6. Back-2-School Kit

The webform also includes a section relating to the Back-2-School Kit (B2SK).

This forms part of the UNICEF Club registration process for the 2026–2027 school year.

7. Confirm and Submit

After completing the required sections, applicants will reach the confirmation and submission stage.

Before submitting, clubs should carefully review the information entered to ensure that it is accurate and complete.

8. Complete

Once the registration process has been successfully submitted, the application enters the UNICEF USA review process.

Applicants should retain any confirmation information provided after submission.

What Happens After You Register?

Submitting the registration form does not mean that the club is immediately approved.

UNICEF USA states that registrations are reviewed by its team.

Once the registration has been approved, the club will receive an approval email within 7–10 business days.

The approval email will include links to helpful resources that can assist the club with its activities.

This means prospective club leaders should monitor the email address provided during registration after submitting their application.

Opportunity to Win UNICEF USA Merchandise

An additional benefit mentioned on the registration page is the opportunity for registered clubs to start winning UNICEF USA merchandise.

This provides an added incentive for clubs to remain engaged and active after completing the registration process.

Students should therefore not view registration simply as an administrative requirement. It can be the starting point for an ongoing school-based effort supporting UNICEF’s mission.

Important Registration Tips

Applicants should pay close attention to UNICEF USA’s instructions when completing the form.

Prepare all information first

Because there is no save-and-return option, do not begin the form until you have collected the required information for:

  • Four club leaders
  • One advisor
  • Your school or organization

Use the form’s Previous button

If you need to return to an earlier section, UNICEF USA specifically advises applicants to use the “previous” button within the form rather than the browser’s back arrow.

This is an important technical instruction because using the browser’s back button could potentially interfere with the form.

Double-check contact information

Make sure names, email addresses, telephone numbers and other requested details are entered correctly.

Incorrect contact information could make it difficult for UNICEF USA to communicate with club leaders or the advisor.

Monitor your email

After submitting the registration, watch the relevant email account for the approval notification.

UNICEF USA indicates that approval emails are expected within 7–10 business days.

Keep your leadership team informed

Since four club leaders and one advisor are required, it is helpful to ensure everyone involved knows that their information is being submitted as part of the official UNICEF Club registration.

Is There a Registration Deadline?

The information provided on the UNICEF USA registration page does not specify a fixed calendar deadline for the 2026–2027 UNICEF Club Registration.

The page simply invites eligible clubs to register for the 2026–2027 school year.

Therefore, applicants should not assume that there is a particular deadline unless UNICEF USA subsequently announces one.

For the most accurate and current registration information, applicants should check the official UNICEF USA registration page before submitting their application.

Registration period: For the 2026–2027 school year; no specific closing date is stated on the provided registration page.

Support and Questions

Applicants who experience problems while completing the registration or have questions about UNICEF Clubs can contact UNICEF USA.

The registration page provides the following email address for assistance:

volunteer@unicefusa.org

This contact is intended for registration issues and other UNICEF Club-related questions.

SMS Notifications

The UNICEF USA website also provides an option for supporters to receive SMS notifications concerning UNICEF’s humanitarian relief efforts during emergencies.

According to the website, individuals who provide their mobile number agree to receive SMS notifications from UNICEF USA.

Message frequency can vary, and standard message and data rates may apply. Users can reply STOP to cancel or HELP for assistance.

The website also provides links to its terms and privacy information relating to SMS notifications.

Why This Opportunity Can Be Valuable for Students

Joining or establishing a UNICEF Club can provide more than simply participation in a school organization.

Students can potentially develop practical skills that are valuable for academic, professional and community leadership.

Leadership experience

Running a student organization requires students to coordinate activities, work with other people and take responsibility for projects.

Communication skills

Club activities can help students practice public speaking, written communication, awareness campaigns and communicating important issues to their peers.

Teamwork

A UNICEF Club requires collaboration between student leaders, members and an advisor.

Project and event organization

Organizing awareness campaigns, school activities and other initiatives can expose students to practical planning and coordination.

Advocacy experience

Students interested in children’s rights, international development and social impact can gain experience communicating important causes and encouraging others to take action.

Community engagement

UNICEF Clubs can give students a platform to connect issues affecting children globally with their own school and local communities.

Who Can Apply?

The opportunity is intended for school-based UNICEF Clubs in the United States, including both new and returning clubs, for the 2026–2027 school year.

The registration information specifically refers to UNICEF Clubs in the USA and requires a school or organization, four club leaders and one advisor.

Therefore, this is not presented as an open global scholarship, fellowship, internship or individual funding opportunity.

Students outside the United States should carefully review the official UNICEF USA requirements before assuming that they can establish a UNICEF USA Club through this registration system.

Geographic Eligibility

Primary geographic scope: United States of America.

The provided registration information is specifically for UNICEF Clubs in the USA.

It does not state that individuals from every country or continent can independently register a UNICEF USA Club through this form.

Applicants outside the United States should contact UNICEF USA directly if they are unsure whether their school or organization qualifies.

Race, Nationality and Equal Participation

The registration information provided does not specify a race, ethnicity or racial restriction.

It also does not identify a particular nationality or ethnic group as the exclusive beneficiary.

The key eligibility distinction described on the page is the club’s connection to a school or organization in the United States, together with the required leadership and advisor information.

Applicants should therefore focus on meeting the stated organizational requirements rather than assuming that the opportunity is restricted to a particular race or ethnicity.

Category of People Who Qualify

The opportunity is primarily relevant to:

  • Students in the United States who want to establish a UNICEF Club.
  • Existing student UNICEF Clubs continuing into the 2026–2027 school year.
  • Four designated student club leaders.
  • A designated school or organization advisor.
  • Schools and student organizations interested in children’s rights and UNICEF-related action.

The provided page does not state a specific minimum age, academic grade, GPA requirement, academic qualification or field of study.

How to Register

Interested applicants should complete the official UNICEF USA Club Registration form HERE for the 2026–2027 school year.

Visit the official website HERE 

Before beginning, make sure you have the required information for four club leaders and one advisor.

Applicants should also remember that the form does not offer a save-and-return option.

Visit the OFY Website HERE for more social clubs

Key Details at a Glance

Conclusion

The UNICEF USA Club Registration for 2026–2027 provides students and school communities in the United States with an opportunity to organize around children’s rights and take meaningful action for children.

Both new and returning clubs must complete the registration process to become active UNICEF Clubs for the new school year. Clubs should prepare the contact information of four club leaders and one advisor before beginning because the registration form does not provide a save-and-return option.

After submission, UNICEF USA states that approved clubs will receive an email within 7–10 business days, along with helpful resources and opportunities to participate in UNICEF USA activities and potentially win UNICEF USA merchandise.

Students interested in leadership, advocacy, children’s rights, community engagement and international development may find the UNICEF Club structure particularly valuable. Anyone considering registration should carefully review the official requirements and submit accurate information through the UNICEF USA registration page.

Important: The provided registration page does not state a fixed application deadline, so prospective clubs should check the official page for any subsequent deadline or registration updates.

item.content:encoded:
The United Nations Development Programme (UNDP) is inviting applications for Agenda 2063 in Power Spaces – Cohort 3, a seven-week online learning and volunteer opportunity designed to help participants strengthen their leadership capacity and identify how they can contribute to achieving Agenda 2063: The Africa We Want.

The programme provides participants with practical tools to move beyond simply understanding Agenda 2063 and instead identify the influence, opportunities and responsibilities they have within their own “Power Spaces” — including governments, businesses, universities, communities, schools, development organizations, families and professional networks.

The opportunity is conducted entirely online and requires approximately 11–15 hours per week.

About the Agenda 2063 in Power Spaces Programme

Agenda 2063 represents Africa’s long-term development vision and focuses on building The Africa We Want. However, achieving this vision requires more than awareness of continental development frameworks.

The UNDP-led programme focuses on helping participants recognize that meaningful transformation can take place through the everyday environments where people make decisions, influence others, and create value.

These environments are referred to as “Power Spaces.”

The programme therefore encourages participants to ask:

  • What contribution can I make to Africa’s transformation?
  • What future am I committed to creating?
  • What needs to change to achieve that future?
  • What leadership values do I need?
  • What actions should I consistently take?
  • What would success look like?
  • How can I continue improving after the programme?

What Participants Will Learn

During the seven-week journey, participants will develop seven practical leadership tools:

1. Contribution Statement

Participants identify the value they currently create through their Power Space and consider how their work, activities or influence can contribute to Africa’s transformation.

2. Moonshot

Participants define an ambitious and meaningful future they are committed to helping create rather than simply accepting current circumstances.

3. Delivery

Participants identify the important changes required to move from their current situation toward their desired future.

4. Leadership Values

Participants explore the values they need to guide important decisions and actions throughout their leadership journey.

5. Leadership Routines

Participants translate their intentions into practical and repeatable behaviours that can gradually produce meaningful results.

6. Letter from the Future

Participants imagine their desired future as if it has already been achieved and use that perspective to reconsider the choices they are making today.

7. Future Review

Participants learn a continuous improvement approach based on:

Return → Review → Revise → Recommit

This enables them to continue using the programme’s leadership tools after the formal seven-week experience has ended.

What Will Online Volunteers Do?

Selected Online Volunteers will participate in the learning experience while also supporting the delivery and improvement of the cohort.

Their responsibilities will include:

  • Studying the Agenda 2063 in Power Spaces Reader and related learning materials.
  • Supporting participant engagement throughout the seven-week programme.
  • Becoming familiar with weekly concepts, questions and exercises.
  • Participating in small-group learning conversations where assigned.
  • Helping participants connect the leadership tools to their own Power Spaces and circumstances.
  • Providing constructive and concise feedback.
  • Contributing to the end-of-cohort review.
  • Identifying what worked well and suggesting areas that could improve future cohorts.

Importantly, applicants do not need to be experts on every aspect of Agenda 2063. The programme emphasizes curiosity, disciplined engagement with the provided materials and the willingness to help others apply the concepts to their own contexts.

Programme Format and Time Commitment

This is a fully online opportunity, meaning volunteers can participate remotely.

Duration: 7 weeks
Modality: Online
Time commitment: 11–15 hours per week
Host organization: United Nations Development Programme (UNDP)
Assignment country: Ethiopia
Sustainable Development Goal: SDG 17 – Partnerships for the Goals
Recruitment: Competitive

The assignment focuses on learning, participant engagement, leadership development and contributing to the improvement of future cohorts.

Who Should Apply?

The opportunity is particularly suitable for people who have a strong interest in areas such as:

  • Agenda 2063 and Africa’s development
  • Leadership and development practice
  • Public policy
  • Business and entrepreneurship
  • Education
  • Community development
  • Social impact
  • African transformation

Applicants may come from different professional and educational backgrounds. The programme specifically welcomes:

  • Professionals
  • Development practitioners
  • Researchers
  • Entrepreneurs
  • Educators
  • Students
  • Community leaders

Applicants should also demonstrate strong written and interpersonal communication skills and the ability to engage critically with learning materials.

Required Skills and Experience

Candidates should demonstrate:

  1. Strong interest in African development and Agenda 2063 or related areas.
  2. Critical reading skills and the ability to engage meaningfully with learning materials.
  3. Strong written and interpersonal communication skills.
  4. Ability to provide concise and constructive feedback.
  5. Commitment to completing the assignment throughout the seven-week Cohort 3 period.

Language Requirement

English: Fluent level is desirable.

Important Application Information

The recruitment is competitive, and applicants should be prepared to commit to the full duration of the assignment.

Application deadline: 4 September 2026 at 03:00.

The programme is expected to run for seven weeks, with participants working remotely and contributing approximately 11–15 hours per week.

Click HERE to read more and apply.

Why This Opportunity Is Valuable

The Agenda 2063 in Power Spaces programme can provide participants with an opportunity to:

  • Develop practical leadership skills.
  • Better understand their potential contribution to Africa’s long-term development.
  • Connect personal leadership with Agenda 2063.
  • Strengthen communication and collaboration skills.
  • Learn how to turn ideas into practical action.
  • Engage with people working across different sectors and Power Spaces.
  • Develop a personal leadership portfolio and future-oriented leadership practice.
  • Contribute feedback that can help improve future cohorts.

The programme is particularly relevant for individuals who want to connect their career, community involvement, education, entrepreneurship or professional influence with broader African development goals.

Conclusion

The UNDP Agenda 2063 in Power Spaces – Cohort 3 offers a structured seven-week online leadership journey for individuals interested in contributing to Africa’s transformation. Rather than focusing only on theoretical knowledge of Agenda 2063, the programme encourages participants to identify their own areas of influence and develop practical ways to create value within them.

With a commitment of 11–15 hours per week and a deadline of 4 September 2026, interested applicants should review the requirements carefully and submit their applications before the recruitment period closes.

Click HERE for more volunteering opportunities.

item.content:encoded:
Agenda 2063 in Power Spaces – Cohort 3

Are you passionate about Africa’s development, leadership, public policy, education, entrepreneurship, community development, or the long-term vision of The Africa We Want? The Agenda 2063 in Power Spaces – Cohort 3 offers an opportunity to take part in a structured seven-week online learning and volunteer experience designed to help participants understand how they can contribute to Africa’s transformation within their own spheres of influence.

Hosted by the United Nations Development Programme (UNDP) and delivered through the wider Agenda 2063 learning ecosystem, the programme focuses on turning knowledge of Agenda 2063 into practical individual leadership and action.

The online assignment is designed for people who want to explore their personal contribution to Africa’s development while supporting other participants during the seven-week traineeship. It does not require applicants to be experts on every aspect of Agenda 2063. Instead, it emphasizes curiosity, critical engagement, communication, willingness to learn, and the ability to help others connect ideas to their own real-world environments.

Opportunity Overview

  • Opportunity Title: Agenda 2063 in Power Spaces – Cohort 3
  • Host Entity: United Nations Development Programme (UNDP)
  • Assignment Country: Ethiopia
  • Modality: Online
  • Duration: 7 weeks
  • Time Commitment: 11–15 hours per week
  • Task Type: Development of plans
  • Relevant Sustainable Development Goal: SDG 17 – Partnerships for the Goals
  • Expected Start Date: The listing does not provide a valid start date
  • Number of Assignments: 0 as indicated in the provided listing
  • Language: English, fluent level desirable
  • Deadline: No application deadline is specified in the provided opportunity details

What Is Agenda 2063?

Agenda 2063 is Africa’s long-term development framework and vision for building “The Africa We Want.” It provides a continental framework for transforming Africa economically, socially and politically while promoting inclusive development, sustainable growth, integration and stronger partnerships.

However, understanding Agenda 2063 as a policy or development framework is only one part of the challenge. Its implementation also depends on the actions of individuals and institutions operating in different environments.

This is the central idea behind Agenda 2063 in Power Spaces.

The programme recognizes that important decisions are made every day in many different environments, including:

  • Governments and public institutions
  • Businesses and private-sector organizations
  • Universities and research institutions
  • Schools and educational organizations
  • Communities and civil society
  • Development organizations
  • Families
  • Professional networks
  • Entrepreneurship and innovation spaces
  • Youth organizations
  • Other environments where people make decisions and create value

These environments are described as “Power Spaces.”

The programme encourages participants to identify the Power Spaces available to them and consider how they can deliberately use those spaces to contribute to Africa’s long-term transformation.

What Is Agenda 2063 in Power Spaces – Cohort 3?

Agenda 2063 in Power Spaces – Cohort 3 is a seven-week online traineeship and volunteer learning experience designed to move participants beyond simply knowing about Agenda 2063.

The programme seeks to help participants answer an important question:

How can I personally contribute to achieving The Africa We Want through the spaces in which I have influence?

Rather than treating leadership as something limited to senior government officials, executives or institutional leaders, the programme takes a broader approach.

It recognizes that individuals can create value and influence outcomes from wherever they operate.

A student can influence a university or student organization. An entrepreneur can influence a business ecosystem. A teacher can influence learners and communities. A researcher can influence policy and knowledge. A community leader can influence local development. A communications professional can influence public awareness and engagement.

The programme therefore focuses on developing individual agency and helping participants recognize themselves as potential contributors to Agenda 2063.

Main Objective of the Programme

The central objective is to help participants progress from understanding Agenda 2063 to recognizing themselves as agents capable of contributing to its implementation.

The seven-week journey provides a structured framework through which participants examine:

  1. The value they currently create.
  2. The future they want to help create.
  3. The changes required to move from the present toward that future.
  4. The leadership values required to make meaningful decisions.
  5. The routines needed to turn intentions into action.
  6. The future they want to experience as a result of their efforts.
  7. The lessons they gain and the changes they need to make going forward.

This makes the programme particularly relevant to people interested in leadership, development practice, public policy, entrepreneurship, education, community development and African transformation.

The Seven Leadership Tools Participants Will Develop

One of the most important features of Agenda 2063 in Power Spaces – Cohort 3 is its seven-tool leadership architecture.

Throughout the seven-week journey, participants progressively work with seven leadership tools.

1. Contribution Statement – What Value Do I Create?

The first tool encourages participants to identify their personal contribution to Africa’s transformation.

Participants examine their current Power Space and consider the value they create within it.

This may involve asking questions such as:

  • What am I currently contributing?
  • Who benefits from my contribution?
  • What capabilities do I possess?
  • What problems am I helping to solve?
  • Where do I have influence?
  • How does my work or activity connect with Africa’s broader development needs?

The Contribution Statement helps participants understand where they currently fit within the broader transformation agenda.

2. Moonshot – What Future Am I Committed to Creating?

The second tool focuses on developing a sufficiently ambitious vision for the future.

The concept of a “Moonshot” encourages participants to think beyond incremental improvements and identify a consequential future they are committed to helping create.

Participants consider:

  • What future do I want to see?
  • What would meaningful transformation look like?
  • What ambitious outcome would challenge current assumptions?
  • What future is worth working toward despite present obstacles?

The exercise is intended to help participants challenge the limitations imposed by present circumstances.

3. Delivery – What Must Change?

Having identified a desired future, participants then examine what needs to change to move toward it.

The Delivery tool focuses on the gap between the current situation and the desired outcome.

Participants may consider:

  • What is preventing progress?
  • Which systems, behaviours or practices need to change?
  • What obstacles must be addressed?
  • Which changes are most critical?
  • What actions can contribute to the desired transformation?

This stage helps translate vision into a practical understanding of what needs to happen.

4. Leadership Values – Who Must I Be?

The fourth tool focuses on the personal qualities and values required to pursue meaningful change.

Participants reflect on the type of leader they need to become in order to make consequential decisions and remain committed to their goals.

This can involve examining:

  • Personal values
  • Integrity
  • Responsibility
  • Courage
  • Accountability
  • Resilience
  • Collaboration
  • Commitment
  • Respect for others
  • Willingness to learn and adapt

The emphasis is not simply on what participants want to achieve but also on who they need to be throughout the journey.

5. Leadership Routines – What Must I Repeatedly Do?

A vision only becomes meaningful when it is translated into consistent action.

The Leadership Routines tool helps participants identify repeated behaviours and practices that can gradually produce results.

Participants consider:

  • What actions must I perform consistently?
  • Which habits will support my goals?
  • What behaviours need to become routine?
  • How can I turn intention into practice?
  • What repeated actions can accumulate into meaningful results?

This stage emphasizes the importance of sustained action rather than one-time motivation.

6. Letter from the Future – What Does Life Look Like Because I Succeeded?

The sixth tool asks participants to imagine their desired future as though they have already achieved it.

Through a Letter from the Future, participants explore what life looks like because their efforts succeeded.

This exercise can help participants:

  • Visualize the impact of their contribution.
  • Understand the consequences of achieving their goals.
  • Reconsider current choices.
  • Identify actions that are consistent with their desired future.
  • Strengthen their connection to their long-term objectives.

The exercise links future aspirations with present-day decision-making.

7. Future Review – What Have I Learned and What Should I Now Revise?

The final tool focuses on reflection, learning and continuous improvement.

Participants are introduced to the practice of:

Return → Review → Revise → Recommit

This process encourages participants to revisit their leadership plans and assess whether their circumstances, experiences and capabilities have changed.

Instead of treating the seven-week programme as an endpoint, participants are encouraged to continue applying the tools after the formal traineeship ends.

What Will Online Volunteers Do?

Online Volunteers will play a supporting role throughout the seven-week traineeship.

Their responsibilities will include the following.

Study the Learning Materials

Volunteers will become familiar with the Agenda 2063 in Power Spaces learning materials, including the Reader and associated resources.

This requires participants to:

  • Read the provided materials.
  • Understand the major concepts.
  • Engage critically with the learning content.
  • Prepare to support participant learning.
  • Develop familiarity with the seven leadership tools.

Volunteers are not expected to arrive as experts. The assignment specifically emphasizes curiosity and disciplined engagement with the materials.

Support Participant Engagement

Volunteers will help support participants throughout the seven-week learning journey.

This involves understanding the weekly concepts, questions and exercises and helping participants remain engaged with the programme.

The emphasis is on supporting learning rather than simply delivering course content.

Participate in Small-Group Learning Conversations

Where assigned, volunteers will participate in small-group conversations.

These discussions are intended to encourage participants to connect the leadership tools to their own Power Spaces.

Volunteers should therefore be capable of:

  • Listening actively.
  • Encouraging participation.
  • Asking constructive questions.
  • Helping participants connect concepts to their own experiences.
  • Providing concise and useful feedback.
  • Supporting a collaborative learning environment.

Contribute to the End-of-Cohort Review

Volunteers will also participate in a structured review at the end of the cohort.

They will help identify:

  • What worked well.
  • What challenges participants experienced.
  • What could be improved.
  • Which learning approaches were effective.
  • How future cohorts could be strengthened.
  • How the materials and participant experience could be improved.

This means volunteers can contribute not only to the current cohort but also to the continued development of the programme.

Who Can Apply?

The opportunity welcomes applications from people with an interest in Africa’s transformation and related areas.

The requirements specifically mention applicants from a variety of professional and educational backgrounds, including:

  • Professionals
  • Development practitioners
  • Researchers
  • Entrepreneurs
  • Educators
  • Students
  • Community leaders

Applicants may come from different sectors and Power Spaces.

The programme is therefore not restricted to one profession or academic discipline.

Required Experience and Skills

Candidates should be able to demonstrate a strong interest in one or more areas connected to Agenda 2063 and African development.

Relevant areas include:

  • Agenda 2063
  • African development
  • Leadership
  • Development practice
  • Public policy
  • Business
  • Education
  • Community development
  • Related fields

Applicants should also demonstrate the following capabilities.

Critical Reading and Learning

Candidates should be comfortable reading learning materials and engaging with them critically.

The programme requires volunteers to understand concepts sufficiently to support discussions and participant engagement.

Strong Written Communication

Good written communication is important because volunteers may need to provide feedback, participate in discussions and communicate ideas clearly.

Strong Interpersonal Communication

The role involves interaction with other participants, particularly through small-group learning conversations.

Applicants should therefore be comfortable communicating respectfully and constructively with people from different backgrounds.

Constructive Feedback

Volunteers should be able to provide feedback that is:

  • Concise
  • Clear
  • Constructive
  • Relevant
  • Helpful to the learning process

Commitment

Applicants must be able to commit to the assignment throughout the seven-week Cohort 3 period.

The expected workload is 11–15 hours per week, making it important for applicants to assess their availability before applying.

Language Requirement

The listed language requirement is:

English – Fluent, desirable.

Applicants should therefore be able to comfortably understand and engage with English-language learning materials and participate effectively in written and interpersonal communication.

Programme Modality and Time Commitment

The assignment is conducted entirely online.

This makes it suitable for participants who can contribute remotely without needing to relocate to Ethiopia or another physical programme location.

The expected commitment is:

11–15 hours per week for seven weeks.

Applicants should ensure they have sufficient time to:

  • Study the learning materials.
  • Participate in learning conversations.
  • Support participant engagement.
  • Complete assigned activities.
  • Contribute to the end-of-cohort review.

What Makes This Opportunity Different?

One of the distinctive features of the programme is that it does not simply present Agenda 2063 as something participants should know.

Instead, it asks participants to consider how they can personally contribute to its implementation.

This approach is important because continental transformation depends not only on governments and large institutions but also on the decisions and actions taken in everyday environments.

The programme’s Power Spaces approach recognizes that individuals have different forms of influence.

A participant does not necessarily need to occupy a senior position to contribute to development.

Their influence could come through:

  • Their profession
  • Their organization
  • Their business
  • Their research
  • Their classroom
  • Their community
  • Their professional network
  • Their family
  • Their youth or civic activities
  • Their educational institution

This makes the programme relevant to participants at different stages of their careers and lives.

Leadership Portfolio and Letter from the Future

Participants are expected to retain important outputs from the learning journey, including their Leadership Portfolio and Letter from the Future.

These materials can serve as practical references after the seven-week programme.

Rather than treating leadership development as a one-time training activity, the programme encourages participants to revisit their materials periodically as their circumstances, experience, capabilities and Power Spaces evolve.

This creates an opportunity for continuous reflection and development.

Contribution to Future Cohorts

Another important aspect of Cohort 3 is its contribution to the continued improvement of the programme.

Participants and volunteers will help test and improve:

  • Learning materials
  • Facilitation approaches
  • Participant engagement methods
  • Overall learning experience
  • Approaches for making the leadership practice accessible to larger numbers of people

Consequently, participation can contribute to the development of future iterations of Agenda 2063 in Power Spaces.

Connection to Sustainable Development Goal 17

The assignment is linked to Sustainable Development Goal 17: Partnerships for the Goals.

SDG 17 emphasizes the importance of partnerships in achieving sustainable development.

The connection is particularly relevant because Agenda 2063 implementation requires collaboration among governments, businesses, communities, civil society, educational institutions, development organizations and individuals.

By encouraging people to identify their Power Spaces and collaborate across different environments, the programme reinforces the importance of partnerships in achieving long-term development objectives.

Is This a Paid Opportunity?

The provided description identifies this as an online volunteer assignment.

It specifically explains that volunteerism involves activities undertaken freely for the public good where monetary reward is not the principal motivating factor.

Therefore, applicants should not approach this as a paid employment opportunity.

The programme is better suited to individuals interested in learning, leadership development, contribution to African development, collaboration and volunteer experience.

Inclusivity and Equal Opportunity

The programme states that United Nations Volunteers is an equal opportunity programme that welcomes qualified applicants.

It is committed to diversity and respect for human rights and individual dignity.

The inclusivity statement specifies that discrimination should not occur on the basis of characteristics including:

  • Race
  • Sex
  • Gender identity
  • Religion
  • Nationality
  • Ethnic origin
  • Sexual orientation
  • Disability
  • Pregnancy
  • Age
  • Language
  • Social origin
  • Other status

The programme therefore emphasizes an inclusive environment in which qualified individuals from diverse backgrounds can participate.

Who Is the Ideal Candidate?

The ideal candidate is someone who is genuinely interested in contributing to Africa’s long-term development and is willing to learn rather than simply demonstrate existing expertise.

A strong applicant could be someone who:

  1. Has an interest in Agenda 2063 and African development.
  2. Is passionate about leadership and positive change.
  3. Can critically read and understand learning materials.
  4. Communicates clearly in English.
  5. Works effectively with other people.
  6. Can provide constructive feedback.
  7. Is comfortable participating in online learning.
  8. Can dedicate 11–15 hours every week for seven weeks.
  9. Is open to learning from people with different experiences.
  10. Can connect abstract ideas with real-world contexts.
  11. Is willing to reflect on their own contribution and leadership.
  12. Wants to continue applying the programme’s tools beyond the formal traineeship.

Benefits of Participating

Although the opportunity is a volunteer assignment rather than a paid position, participants can gain several forms of professional and personal value.

Leadership Development

The seven-tool framework provides participants with a structured approach to examining their contribution, aspirations, values, routines and future goals.

Understanding of Agenda 2063

Participants gain an opportunity to engage directly with Agenda 2063 and explore its relevance to individual action and African transformation.

Practical Reflection

The programme goes beyond theoretical learning by encouraging participants to apply the concepts to their own Power Spaces.

Collaboration

Small-group learning conversations provide opportunities to engage with people from different professional, educational and community backgrounds.

Communication Skills

Supporting discussions and providing constructive feedback can strengthen written and interpersonal communication.

Development Perspective

The programme can help participants connect individual leadership with broader development objectives.

International Volunteer Experience

Participation in an online UN-linked volunteer assignment can provide experience of contributing to an international development-oriented initiative.

How to Prepare for the Opportunity

Applicants interested in this programme should carefully consider how their existing experience connects with the assignment.

Before applying, it can be useful to reflect on the following questions:

  • What does Agenda 2063 mean to me?
  • What aspect of African development interests me most?
  • What Power Space do I currently operate in?
  • What value do I create in that space?
  • What development challenge would I like to help address?
  • What leadership qualities do I already demonstrate?
  • What leadership qualities do I need to strengthen?
  • Can I dedicate 11–15 hours per week for seven weeks?
  • Can I effectively communicate and collaborate with people online?
  • How could my professional, academic, entrepreneurial or community experience contribute to the programme?

Applicants should also ensure that their application clearly demonstrates their motivation, relevant interests, communication abilities and commitment.

Important Scam Warning

Applicants should be particularly careful about fraudulent individuals or websites claiming to represent the United Nations.

The opportunity information explicitly warns that the United Nations does not charge application, processing, training, interviewing, testing or recruitment fees.

If anyone requests money in exchange for applying, being shortlisted, receiving training or securing recruitment, applicants should disregard the request.

Applicants should also exercise caution when submitting personal information online because logos, names, addresses and other organizational materials can be copied and reproduced by scammers.

Always verify that an application is being submitted through the legitimate United Nations or UN Volunteers recruitment platform.

Application Deadline

No application deadline is specified in the opportunity information provided.

Applicants should therefore check the official listing for the current application status and any deadline or closing date before submitting an application.

The provided listing also shows an invalid/unspecified expected start date, so applicants should verify the latest programme schedule through the official recruitment platform.

APPLY HERE

Conclusion

The Agenda 2063 in Power Spaces – Cohort 3 provides an opportunity to engage with Africa’s long-term development vision from a personal and practical leadership perspective.

Its central message is that achieving The Africa We Want is not solely the responsibility of governments or major institutions. Transformation can also emerge from the many Power Spaces in which individuals learn, work, build businesses, conduct research, educate others, participate in communities and make decisions.

Over seven weeks, participants will explore seven practical leadership tools covering contribution, vision, delivery, values, routines, future thinking and continuous review. They will also support other learners, participate in group conversations and contribute feedback that can improve future cohorts.

For professionals, students, researchers, entrepreneurs, educators, practitioners and community leaders interested in Africa’s development, this online volunteer assignment can provide a structured opportunity to deepen their understanding of Agenda 2063 while reflecting on how their own work and influence can contribute to the continent’s transformation.

With a commitment of 11–15 hours per week for seven weeks, applicants should ensure that they have sufficient time and motivation to participate fully. Most importantly, successful participation requires more than familiarity with development terminology. It requires curiosity, critical thinking, communication, collaboration and a genuine willingness to connect ideas with action.

The programme ultimately encourages participants to move from asking “What is Agenda 2063?” toward a more personal and consequential question: “What can I contribute to achieving The Africa We Want through the Power Spaces available to me?”

item.content:encoded:
The Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations (FAO) is inviting eligible applicants to submit expressions of interest for the FAO Regular Volunteer Programme for Africa (RAF) 2026. This international volunteer opportunity gives individuals an avenue to contribute their knowledge, experience, research background and skills to the work of one of the United Nations’ specialized agencies while supporting efforts to combat hunger, malnutrition and food insecurity.

Published under Vacancy Announcement No. 2600018, the programme is a non-staff volunteer opportunity with assignments available in various locations. Successful candidates may serve for a period of up to a maximum of six months, working in fields relevant to FAO’s mandate and activities.

The programme is particularly relevant to individuals interested in agriculture, food security, nutrition, sustainable development and other areas connected with FAO’s work. Applicants must be at least 18 years old, have completed secondary school education and meet FAO’s language and nationality requirements.

Importantly, this is an unpaid volunteer programme. FAO explicitly states that volunteers do not receive remuneration.

FAO Regular Volunteer Programme for Africa 2026 at a Glance

Key information about the opportunity includes:

  • Organization: Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations (FAO)
  • Programme: FAO Regular Volunteer Programme for Africa (RAF)
  • Vacancy Announcement Number: 2600018
  • Organizational Unit: RAF
  • Opportunity Type: Non-staff opportunity
  • Requisition Type: Volunteer Programme
  • Grade Level: N/A
  • Primary Location: Various locations
  • Duration: Up to a maximum of six months
  • Posting Date: January 25, 2026
  • Application Deadline: August 26, 2026, at 9:59 AM, subject to the date and time settings of the applicant’s personal device
  • Minimum Age: 18 years
  • Minimum Education: Completed secondary school education
  • Remuneration: None; FAO does not provide remuneration to volunteers
  • Application Method: Online through the official FAO recruitment portal

Applicants are strongly encouraged to submit their applications well ahead of the closing date rather than waiting until the final day.

Application Deadline for the FAO Volunteer Programme 2026

The application deadline for the FAO Regular Volunteer Programme for Africa is August 26, 2026, at 9:59 AM.

FAO notes that the closure date and time displayed on its recruitment platform are based on the date and time settings of the applicant’s personal device. Applicants should therefore carefully check the deadline shown when accessing the official recruitment portal.

Submitting an application early is highly recommended. This provides applicants with enough time to complete their online profile, upload the required documents, verify their employment and educational information, and address any technical issues before applications close.

About the Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations

The Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations is a specialized agency of the United Nations that leads international efforts to defeat hunger and achieve food security.

FAO works toward a world where people have regular access to sufficient quantities of high-quality food that enable them to live active and healthy lives.

With more than 195 Members and operations spanning over 130 countries, FAO works internationally on challenges connected to agriculture, food systems, hunger, nutrition, rural development and sustainable development.

The organization believes that individuals can contribute to the global effort to end hunger, which is one of the ideas underpinning its Regular Volunteer Programme.

What Is the FAO Regular Volunteer Programme?

The FAO Regular Volunteer Programme creates opportunities for individuals to contribute volunteer services to areas that support FAO’s mission.

Where appropriate, volunteer contributions are connected to the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) and FAO’s Strategic Framework, supporting the implementation of the 2030 Agenda.

A major focus of FAO’s work is the transformation toward more efficient, inclusive, resilient and sustainable agri-food systems.

This transformation is organized around the aspirations of:

  • Better production
  • Better nutrition
  • A better environment
  • A better life

The broader objective is to achieve these improvements while leaving no one behind.

Through the Regular Volunteer Programme, FAO seeks to strategically mobilize volunteer services from citizens of its Member countries. Their contributions can support the organization’s work toward ending hunger, malnutrition and food insecurity.

What Will FAO Volunteers Do?

Successful applicants will be assigned to areas relevant to the mission and work of FAO.

The exact duties will depend on the assignment and the needs of the hiring office.

According to the vacancy announcement, each volunteer will perform functions specified in the Terms of Reference (TOR) prepared by the hiring office.

This means applicants should not assume that every volunteer will perform exactly the same duties. Responsibilities may vary depending on factors such as the candidate’s expertise, the field of assignment, the location, organizational priorities and the specific FAO office involved.

Reporting Arrangements

Each selected volunteer will report to an assigned supervisor.

The supervisor will provide the relevant oversight for the volunteer’s assignment and the duties specified under the applicable Terms of Reference.

Technical Focus of the Programme

Volunteers will be assigned to fields that are relevant to FAO’s work and mission.

FAO also identifies relevant working or research experience in one of the fields of the Organization as an important technical or functional skill.

Applicants with relevant experience should therefore make sure their online profiles clearly explain their work, research and other applicable experience.

Eligibility Requirements for the FAO Regular Volunteer Programme for Africa

Candidates will be assessed against a number of minimum requirements.

1. Education Requirement

Applicants must have completed secondary school education.

This establishes the minimum educational threshold for the programme.

Applicants are also requested to provide a copy of their academic qualifications as part of their online application profile.

2. Minimum Age Requirement

Candidates must be 18 years of age or older.

The announcement does not specify an upper age limit.

3. Nationality Requirement

Applicants must be nationals of FAO Member countries.

Prospective candidates should verify that their country is an FAO Member before submitting an application.

FAO additionally encourages applications from qualified nationals of non- and under-represented Members.

4. Language Requirement

Candidates must have a working knowledge of at least one FAO language.

FAO’s listed languages for this opportunity are:

  • Arabic
  • Chinese
  • English
  • French
  • Russian
  • Spanish

Knowledge of a second FAO language is considered an asset.

Applicants should accurately provide their language abilities when completing their FAO online profile because applications are screened based on the information submitted.

5. Ability to Work in a Multicultural Environment

Candidates should be able to adapt to an international multicultural environment.

This requirement reflects the international nature of FAO and its workforce, which brings together people of different nationalities, professional backgrounds and cultures.

6. Communication Skills

Applicants should possess good communication skills.

Communication is also included among FAO’s core competencies for candidates.

7. Relevant Work or Research Experience

FAO identifies relevant working or research experience in one of the fields of the Organization as a technical or functional skill for this opportunity.

Applicants with such experience should ensure it is clearly reflected in their profiles.

FAO Core Competencies

Applicants will also be considered in relation to FAO’s core competencies.

These include:

  1. Results Focus – the ability to remain focused on delivering meaningful outcomes and contributing effectively toward objectives.
  2. Teamwork – the capacity to collaborate productively with colleagues and others.
  3. Communication – the ability to communicate information effectively in a professional environment.
  4. Building Effective Relationships – the capacity to establish and maintain constructive working relationships.
  5. Knowledge Sharing and Continuous Improvement – a commitment to sharing useful knowledge and continuously developing and improving professional practices.

Applicants should consider demonstrating these competencies through the experiences described in their online profiles and motivation letters.

FAO Values Expected From Candidates

All candidates are expected to adhere to FAO’s organizational values, including:

  • Commitment to FAO
  • Respect for All
  • Integrity and Transparency

FAO also requires everyone working for the organization to uphold high standards of integrity and professional conduct.

Who Is Particularly Encouraged to Apply?

FAO emphasizes workforce diversity in relation to gender, nationality, background and culture.

The organization particularly encourages applications from:

  • Qualified female applicants
  • Qualified nationals of non- and under-represented FAO Members
  • Persons with disabilities
  • Candidates from Low-Income Food-Deficit Countries (LIFDCs)
  • Candidates from Least Developed Countries (LDCs)
  • Candidates from Land-locked Developing Countries (LLDCs)
  • Candidates from Small Island Developing States (SIDS)

Being encouraged to apply should not be confused with automatically being selected. Candidates must still meet the programme requirements and go through FAO’s assessment and selection process.

Important Family Employment Restriction

Applicants should carefully note an important eligibility restriction.

Candidates who have certain family members employed by FAO under any type of contractual arrangement are not eligible for the FAO Regular Volunteer Programme.

For this requirement, FAO defines the relevant family members as:

  • Mother
  • Father
  • Sister
  • Brother
  • Daughter
  • Son

Applicants affected by this restriction should take it into account before submitting an application.

Is the FAO Regular Volunteer Programme Paid?

No. FAO does not provide remuneration to volunteers.

This is an important consideration for anyone interested in applying.

Applicants should understand the financial implications of participating in an unpaid volunteer programme, particularly if an assignment involves relocation or living in another country.

Candidates should therefore carefully evaluate their circumstances and any assignment-specific requirements before accepting an offer if selected.

Immigration and Residence Requirements

Selected candidates must have the appropriate residence or immigration status in the proposed country of assignment before joining FAO.

This requirement is especially important for candidates who may be considered for an assignment outside their current place of residence.

Applicants should pay close attention to any information provided by FAO concerning the proposed country of assignment if they progress through the selection process.

Selection and Assessment Process

FAO states that all applications will be reviewed, but only qualified applicants will be directly contacted by the hiring office for interviews.

Applicants who are subsequently selected will be contacted again.

Candidates should therefore ensure that their contact details and profile information are accurate and current.

FAO also states that all selected candidates will undergo rigorous reference and background checks.

Applications are treated with strict confidentiality.

How to Apply for the FAO Regular Volunteer Programme for Africa 2026

Applications must be submitted through the official Jobs at FAO recruitment portal.

Applicants should follow these steps:

Step 1: Visit the FAO Recruitment Website

Access the official Jobs at FAO recruitment website and locate the Call for Expression of Interest for the FAO Regular Volunteer Programme for Africa under Vacancy Announcement No. 2600018.

Step 2: Create or Update Your Online Profile

Candidates must complete their online FAO profile.

FAO strongly recommends ensuring that the profile is accurate and complete.

Particular attention should be given to information concerning:

  • Employment history
  • Academic qualifications
  • Language skills
  • Relevant professional experience
  • Relevant research experience

Because applications will be screened based on the information contained in the online profile, candidates should make sure important qualifications and experience are not omitted.

Step 3: Prepare a Motivation Letter

Applicants are requested to attach a letter of motivation to their online profile.

The motivation letter is an opportunity to explain why the candidate wants to volunteer with FAO and how their background, experience and interests are relevant to the organization’s work.

Applicants should ensure that their motivation letter accurately represents their experience and reasons for applying.

Step 4: Attach Academic Qualifications

Candidates are also requested to attach a copy of their academic qualifications.

Applicants should ensure that the documents correspond with the educational information entered in their online profile.

Step 5: Review the Application

Before submitting, applicants should carefully review their profile and documents.

Check that:

  • Personal information is correct.
  • Employment records are complete.
  • Academic information is accurate.
  • Language abilities are properly listed.
  • Relevant experience has been included.
  • The motivation letter is attached.
  • Academic qualification documents are attached.
  • All required sections of the application have been completed.

Step 6: Submit Through the FAO Portal

Once the profile is complete, candidates must formally apply and submit their application.

Only applications received through the FAO recruitment portal will be considered.

Applications submitted through unofficial channels should therefore not be relied upon as a substitute for the formal online application.

Step 7: Apply Before the Deadline

Candidates should submit their applications well before August 26, 2026, at 9:59 AM, taking into account that the closure time displayed by FAO is based on the date and time settings of the applicant’s personal device.

APPLY NOW

Incomplete Applications Will Not Be Considered

Applicants should take the application requirements seriously because FAO states that incomplete applications will not be considered.

Candidates should avoid submitting a partially completed profile with the intention of adding important information after the deadline.

Since screening is based on information contained in the online profile, the quality and completeness of the application can be important to the assessment process.

What Happens to Applicant Information?

FAO explains that personal information provided as part of an application may be shared internally within FAO and with companies working on FAO’s behalf to provide employment-support services.

These services can include:

  • Pre-screening of applications
  • Assessment tests
  • Background checks
  • Other related recruitment support services

Candidates will be asked to provide consent before submitting their applications.

Applicants may withdraw their consent by withdrawing their application. However, if an application is withdrawn, FAO will no longer be able to consider the candidate for the opportunity.

What Happens If You Are Not Selected Before the Closing Date?

Candidates who are not selected before the closing date but want to continue being considered for future assignments will need to re-apply to new Calls for Expression of Interest.

Applicants should therefore not assume that an application under this call will remain active indefinitely for future volunteer opportunities.

FAO Does Not Charge Recruitment Fees

Applicants should be aware that FAO does not charge a fee at any stage of its recruitment process.

This includes:

  • Application
  • Interview
  • Processing

Candidates should be cautious about anyone requesting payment while claiming that a fee is required to secure an FAO volunteer position or advance an application.

Official applications should be submitted through FAO’s recruitment system.

FAO’s Standards of Conduct

FAO maintains a zero-tolerance policy toward conduct incompatible with its status, objectives and mandate.

This includes:

  • Sexual exploitation and abuse
  • Sexual harassment
  • Abuse of authority
  • Discrimination

Individuals selected to work with FAO are expected to uphold the organization’s professional and ethical standards.

Why the FAO Regular Volunteer Programme Matters

The FAO Regular Volunteer Programme provides a structured avenue through which eligible individuals can contribute to international efforts addressing some of the world’s most significant food and agricultural challenges.

Rather than being limited to a single standardized role, volunteers may be assigned to fields that correspond with FAO’s mission and the requirements of individual hiring offices.

The programme connects volunteer participation with FAO’s broader efforts to transform agri-food systems and advance the 2030 Agenda and Sustainable Development Goals.

For candidates interested in contributing to international development, food security, sustainable agriculture, nutrition and related fields, the programme represents an opportunity to support the work of a major United Nations specialized agency.

Applicants should nevertheless carefully consider that the programme is unpaid and that selected candidates are responsible for having appropriate residence or immigration status in the proposed country of assignment before joining FAO.

Important Details to Remember Before Applying

Prospective applicants should remember the following:

  1. The programme is open to eligible nationals of FAO Member countries.
  2. Applicants must be at least 18 years old.
  3. Candidates must have completed secondary school education.
  4. A working knowledge of at least one FAO language is required.
  5. Knowledge of a second FAO language is an advantage.
  6. Candidates should be able to work effectively in an international multicultural environment.
  7. Good communication skills are expected.
  8. Relevant work or research experience in an FAO field is valuable.
  9. A motivation letter and copy of academic qualifications should be attached to the online profile.
  10. Applications must be complete and submitted through the official FAO recruitment portal.
  11. The volunteer programme does not provide remuneration.
  12. Selected candidates must have appropriate residence or immigration status for the proposed country of assignment before joining FAO.
  13. Selected candidates will undergo reference and background checks.
  14. Certain candidates with immediate family members employed by FAO are not eligible.
  15. FAO does not charge an application, interview or processing fee.
  16. The application deadline is August 26, 2026, at 9:59 AM, subject to the applicant’s device date and time settings.

Conclusion

The FAO Regular Volunteer Programme for Africa 2026 offers eligible individuals an opportunity to contribute their time, knowledge and experience to the work of the Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations.

Through assignments of up to six months, selected volunteers can support fields connected with FAO’s mission while contributing to broader international efforts to address hunger, malnutrition and food insecurity and advance more efficient, inclusive, resilient and sustainable agri-food systems.

Applicants must meet the minimum eligibility conditions, including being at least 18 years old, having completed secondary school education, being a national of an FAO Member country and having working knowledge of at least one of FAO’s six listed languages. Candidates should also be capable of working in an international multicultural environment and possess good communication skills.

Prospective applicants should be especially aware that this is an unpaid volunteer opportunity, and FAO does not provide remuneration to volunteers. Selected candidates must also have the appropriate residence or immigration status for their proposed country of assignment before joining the organization.

Those who meet the requirements should carefully complete their FAO online profile, include accurate employment, educational and language information, attach their motivation letter and academic qualifications, and submit a complete application through the official FAO recruitment portal.

The deadline to apply for the FAO Regular Volunteer Programme for Africa is August 26, 2026, at 9:59 AM, with the displayed closing time based on the date and time settings of the applicant’s personal device. Candidates are strongly encouraged to apply well before the deadline.

For further information https://fao.service-now.com/csp
